name: DeepSeek (Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co.)
monetization: Open-weight frontier models (V-series, R-series) monetized through ultra-cheap API pricing; historically bankrolled by founder Liang Wenfeng's High-Flyer hedge fund rather than outside capital.
description_md: DeepSeek is the Hangzhou lab, spun out of and funded by Liang Wenfeng's quantitative hedge fund High-Flyer, whose January 2025 R1 release triggered the largest one-day market-cap loss in history (Nvidia, ~$600B) by demonstrating frontier-adjacent capability at a fraction of assumed training cost. Its April 2026 V4 family (1.6T-parameter MoE Pro; 284B Flash) was trained and served on Huawei Ascend hardware from day 0 — making DeepSeek the flagship proof of China's domestic compute stack. It open-sources weights and prices its API far below Western labs, repeatedly resetting global price-performance expectations.
ai_monetization_md: Revenue comes from API access priced aggressively below Western labs (V4 continued the pattern of order-of-magnitude-cheaper tokens) and from the halo it provides High-Flyer; weights are open, so DeepSeek captures none of the self-hosted usage it enables. No revenue figures are disclosed and press estimates are unreliable (its consumer app had ~127M MAU in March 2026 per QuestMobile, third in China behind Doubao and Qwen). The economics were historically irrelevant by design — High-Flyer funded it as a research vehicle — which is precisely why the June 2026 reports of a $7.4B external raise at >$50B valuation mark a regime change, if accurate.
ai_strategy_md: Maximize capability per unit of compute under export-control constraints (sparse MoE architectures, aggressive engineering), publish weights to commoditize rivals' pricing and win the global open-weights ecosystem, and anchor the domestic hardware stack (V4 day-0 on Ascend, co-optimized with Huawei). The reported 2026 funding round — led by Tencent (~$1.5B) with CATL (~$735M), structured as a Liang-controlled limited partnership with a five-year lockup and no investor voting rights except China's state AI fund — would fund scaling while preserving total founder control.
risk_notes_md: **Valuation/funding uncertainty — confidence low:** the '>$50B valuation / $7.4B raise' reports (The Information, Jun 2026, widely re-reported) conflict with DeepSeek's documented history of refusing external capital, and the unusual LP structure means investors hold economic exposure, not equity in the operating company; the company has not confirmed the round. Record both the claims and the conflict, not a resolved fact. **Export-control frame:** DeepSeek is the demand-side anchor of the Ascend ecosystem after the H20 ban→re-license (15% USG revenue share)→B30A blockade sequence and the Jun 1, 2026 offshore-DC ban; its ceiling is now Huawei/SMIC's manufacturing ceiling. **Key-person/single-backer:** Liang Wenfeng controls research direction and (via High-Flyer/the LP) the funding; no independent governance. **Monetization:** open weights + rock-bottom API pricing may never support frontier-scale capex without state or strategic subsidy.

observations.notes: Reported first-ever external round (~RMB 50B): Tencent ~$1.5B, CATL ~$735M, others via a Liang-controlled LP (5-yr lockup, no voting rights; state AI fund invested directly with voting rights). Unconfirmed by the company; conflicts with its no-external-capital history — hence low confidence.
'More than $50B' per reports of the same round; single primary source (The Information) behind most coverage. Treat as a claim under verification, not an established mark.
V4 Pro: 1.6T total / ~49B active parameters; V4 Flash: 284B. Trained and served on Huawei Ascend from day 0; open weights; priced far below Western frontier APIs.
Third in China's AI-native apps behind ByteDance's Doubao (345M) and Alibaba's Qwen (166M), per QuestMobile Q1 2026.

events.title: R1 release triggers global AI-stock selloff; Nvidia sheds ~$600B in one day
events.why_it_matters: Established that training-cost assumptions underpinning Western capex could be wrong — the single largest market event of the AI cycle to that date, and DeepSeek's entry into systemic relevance.

events.title: V4 launches: 1.6T-parameter MoE, trained and served on Huawei Ascend from day 0
events.why_it_matters: Decoupled China's flagship open-weight lab from Nvidia hardware entirely, validating the domestic stack under export controls and again undercutting global API pricing.

events.title: First external funding reported: ~$7.4B at >$50B valuation via LP structure (unconfirmed)
events.why_it_matters: If accurate, ends the High-Flyer-only funding era while preserving Liang's control through a no-voting-rights LP; reporting rests largely on one outlet and conflicts with the lab's history — recorded at low confidence.

sources.notes: Export-control frame relevant to DeepSeek's Ascend dependence.
